name: Pan-Asianism
summary: Pan-Asianism holds that the peoples of Asia share a common civilization and should cooperate or unite politically against Western imperialism and colonial domination. It arose in the late 19th century and drew support from Japanese, Chinese, Indian and other thinkers. Its Japanese strand increasingly claimed leadership of Asia and became the justification for expansion under the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, while Sun Yat-sen's version called for a moral alliance of equals.
scope: The classical Pan-Asianism of the late 19th century to 1945: Okakura's spiritual 'Asia is one' thesis, Konoe's Asian Monroe Doctrine, Sun Yat-sen's 1924 Greater Asianism speech, and the 1943 Greater East Asia declaration. It excludes the modern Asian-values and leftist Wang Hui revivals except where noted. Most statements sit outside the movement's concerns, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pan-Asianism had no health program; wartime Japanese and Sun's developmentalist versions assumed an active state, so a mild yes is inferred from that.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Pan-Asian writings concern geopolitics and civilization, not wage law, and adherents ranged from state-capitalists to socialists, so the movement is split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Co-Prosperity Sphere was a managed bloc in which colonies served as resource reservoirs, implying planned, state-directed exchange over free markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Strands differ: Wang Hui's version leans social-democratic while Japanese wartime planning mixed state control with private firms; no common line is documented.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation of the rich was not a Pan-Asian concern and adherents spanned Meiji nationalists, Sun's socialist-leaning followers and Asian-values conservatives.

unions-good.rationale: No Pan-Asian text addresses unions; wartime Japanese versions subordinated labor to the state while Sun's followers and Wang Hui's strand were friendlier to workers.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights were not a defining Pan-Asian question; the movement's wartime form overrode property in occupied lands while others were conventional.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Business regulation is not addressed; the Sphere envisaged state-guided economic cooperation but there is no documented position on corporate regulation as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare policy sits outside the movement's concerns, and no documented Pan-Asian position exists either way.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership appears in no Pan-Asian source; mainstream strands (Meiji nationalists, the 1943 declaration's state-led development) favored state or national organization of the economy.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Mainstream Pan-Asianism was tied to security-minded nationalist states, and its Asian-values heirs accept state order over individual privacy; inferred, not stated.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred: Okakura-style cultural traditionalism and Asian-values conservatism favor social order; Western opium trade was itself a grievance in the anti-imperial case.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech law is not discussed; the 1943 declaration condemned racial discrimination but the movement itself used racial rhetoric (Sun's 'Yellow race').

strong-leader.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism sought a leading state to guide Asia, and its Asian-values heirs (Lee Kuan Yew, Mahathir) favor strong executive leadership; inferred for domestic politics.

state-harmful.rationale: Implied: Pan-Asianism is a state-building and alliance project seeking sovereignty for Asian nations, though the sources never debate the state as such.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun policy is irrelevant to the movement and no adherent position is documented.

empower-police-military.rationale: Resisting Western domination was framed as needing strong national power, and Japanese strands built on military strength; inferred rather than stated as a program.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist Asian-values and cultural-defense strands; Pan-Asianism itself did not address it.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement favored larger regional unity and strong national or Japan-led authority over local decentralization; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is outside Pan-Asian concerns and no common position is documented.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the movement's claim that Asian civilizations hold values distinct from the West's; no source on classical Pan-Asianism discusses family structure.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from its Asian-values and cultural-traditionalist strands, which resist Western social liberalism; the classical movement did not discuss it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by any Pan-Asian source and adherents' views differ by country and era.

more-religion-public.rationale: Okakura saw a shared Asian spiritual impulse behind the great religions, but Pan-Asianism was not a program for religion in public life and spanned secular and religious figures.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial equality at the world level mattered (the 1943 declaration and the failed 1919 equality proposal) but domestic redress programs were not a theme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No Pan-Asian source addresses gender theory; traditionalist strands would resist it but the question is anachronistic for the classical movement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending Asian cultures and traditions against Western influence is a core theme, and the 1943 declaration pledged respect for each nation's traditions.

gradual-change.rationale: Pan-Asianists ranged from Meiji-era reformers and Sun's revolutionaries to radical Japanese expansionists, so there is no shared view on pace of change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration control was not a Pan-Asian issue; indeed its grievance included Western restrictions on Asian immigrants such as the 1924 US Act.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pan-Asianism challenged a Western-dominated world order such as the Washington System and League, preferring regional bodies; global organizations were seen as Western instruments.

free-trade.rationale: Sphere-style regional blocs and resistance to Western commercial domination point against open global trade, though intra-Asian trade was welcomed; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: The movement placed regional solidarity ahead of narrow national interest in its ideals, though critics note Japanese versions put Japan first; the stated position is for Asian cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Wartime Japanese use of 'liberation' rhetoric was widely seen as pretext, and the movement stressed sovereignty and non-Western interference; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Pan-Asianism sought a bloc of sovereign Asian nations with Asia set apart from the West, not open borders globally.

limit-growth.rationale: The movement sought economic development and catching up with the West; Asian-values heirs champion growth. Inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for the classical movement and not a theme in sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Okakura contrasted Asian spirituality with Western materialism while Japan's Pan-Asianism embraced modernization; adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Sun Yat-sen, a revolutionary, was a leading Pan-Asianist, and Indian and other anti-colonial strands backed overthrowing foreign rule.

experts-over-public.rationale: No documented stance; Asian-values strands favor elite guidance while Sun stressed popular sovereignty.

central-planning.rationale: Wartime Japanese planning for the Sphere used heavy state direction but Pan-Asianism has no doctrine on planned versus market economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed in any source and strands differ on economic systems.

land-value-tax.rationale: Sun favored land value taxation, but it was not a Pan-Asian doctrine and the question lies outside the movement.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic self-strengthening against Western dominance suggests protection of Asian industry; inferred from the anti-imperial and bloc-building aims.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Sphere and Asian-values developmental states practiced state-guided investment; inferred as the typical orientation.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No Pan-Asian strand sought a moneyless society; even the leftist version proposed social democracy, per Wang Hui.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Pan-Asian states pursued state-led economies; abolishing central banks is foreign to the movement. Inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Wartime Japan had corporatist organizations, but Pan-Asianism as a doctrine does not prescribe them.

one-party-rule.rationale: Strands split: Japan's wartime unified party, Sun's Kuomintang tutelage and Asian-values one-party dominance versus Indian and other democratic figures.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism was centered on the emperor system (hakkō ichiu) and Asian-values heirs include monarchies; though Sun was a republican. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

democracy-best.rationale: Inferred: advocates saw European models as lacking Asian values, but Sun Yat-sen was a republican democrat, and Wang Hui's rejection of multi-party democracy is a modern, out-of-scope strand.

workers-councils.rationale: Only Wang Hui's strand leans leftward and it keeps a social democracy; councils are not part of the movement.

right-to-secede.rationale: Japan's version annexed Korea and Taiwan and the movement prized unity; Pan-Asianism asserts national self-determination vs outsiders, not regional secession. Inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism claimed Japan was the natural guide and leader of Asia, a hierarchical ordering; applied to people it is inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Adherents backed anti-imperial war, and secret societies like the Black Dragon Society used force; Sun framed it as resistance to Western might.

war-builds-character.rationale: Wartime strands glorified struggle, but Sun's Kingly Way contrasts with rule by might; the movement is divided.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion-state relations are not a Pan-Asian question; strands from Shinto-state Japan to secular Chinese republicans differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Pan-Asianism treats religion as a shared cultural-spiritual heritage (Okakura), not a basis for law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Pan-Asianism is about strong states and regional alliances for defense against Western powers, so private defense is unthinkable. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

military-superiority.rationale: Japan's pre-war version justified military strength to resist the Western powers, and Asian Monroeism sought exclusive regional dominance.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sun spoke of a 'Yellow race' bloc, but the Sphere comprised multi-ethnic states and Japan ruled over other peoples; no common nation-state ethnic doctrine.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mainstream Pan-Asianism framed history as a struggle of Asia against Western imperialism, not of classes; Li Dazhao's critical strand differs.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, and Japanese expansion overrode local peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonialism is central, but reparations from Western powers were not a stated demand in the documented sources; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement's core claim is that Asians share a heritage and should unite politically, as Okakura wrote 'Asia is one'.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Asian-values and Okakura's critique of Western materialism and Sun's moral Kingly Way favor community over self-interest; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from the contrast Pan-Asianists drew between Asian and Western values; the sources name no classical position on duties versus individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Okakura's spiritual outlook is sometimes read as harmonious with nature, but no political position is stated.

limit-population.rationale: Population control is absent from Pan-Asian writings, though some Japanese expansionists cited crowding as a motive for expansion.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Okakura criticized Western materialism, but Pan-Asianism overall sought modernization to compete with the West.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Meiji Japan modernized quickly while others were cautious; no common doctrine.

restore-past-order.rationale: Okakura and Asian-values strands defended heritage, but the movement also pushed modern state building and rebirth; split.

direct-action.rationale: Secret societies and Sun's revolutionary action coexisted with elite diplomacy and alliance-building; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Sun's rule-of-virtue ideal suggests moral means, but Japanese expansionist strands used force in the name of liberation, so no shared stance exists.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Implied by the movement's pursuit of modern state power and industrial strength for Asia; a hunter-gatherer life is never considered in the sources.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: No Pan-Asian strand proposes this; the Sphere aimed at an Asian division of resources and industry. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed beyond some leftist strands.

production-for-use.rationale: The sources describe the Sphere as resource extraction for Japan, not a needs-based production doctrine, and give no position on this.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist theory is not Pan-Asian doctrine, though Li Dazhao's critical strand and Wang Hui's leftist version diverge from the mainstream.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Mainstream Pan-Asianism was nationalist and civilizational, and Li Dazhao-style critics were separate from it.

collective-farming.rationale: No Pan-Asian source discusses farm organization; Sun's land reform ideas were separate from the movement's program.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pan-Asianists blamed Western imperialism for aggression, though not as a Marxist law of capitalism; Li Dazhao's critical strand differs.

taxation-theft.rationale: Pan-Asianism builds on strong states and developmental aims, so rejecting taxation is foreign to it. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

harm-principle.rationale: Asian-values strands subordinate individual liberty to community order; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement stressed collective Asian identity and community obligations against Western individualism.

conscription.rationale: Wartime Japanese strands and Asian Monroeist security thinking assume national mobilization; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Pan-Asianism stresses solidarity and loyalty, not exit; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: sources describe state-led developmental and duty-based visions rather than customer-style governance.

positive-liberty.rationale: The question of material means for freedom is not discussed; the movement's notion of freedom is national liberation from Western domination.

media-academia-power.rationale: Pan-Asian sources do not discuss universities or news media as political powers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial claims were made about Yellow-race solidarity and Okakura's temperaments, but not as genetic ability differences, and Sun spoke against Western might.

organic-representation.rationale: Not documented; Japan's wartime corporatist bodies existed but are not Pan-Asian doctrine.

total-state.rationale: Wartime Japan's mobilization shaped one strand, but the ideals of the movement were regional cooperation, not total state control.

national-rebirth.rationale: Pan-Asianism claimed Asia must awaken from Western domination to restore its status, as in Sun's 'restore the status of the Asian peoples'.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Japanese wartime Pan-Asianism expanded by force and critics see it as imperialist, while Sun and the classical strand wanted cooperation among equals; deeply split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal-style oath-based rule is not a Pan-Asian doctrine, though Japanese imperial loyalty ideology was invoked in the wartime strand.

bound-labor.rationale: No Pan-Asian document supports serfdom; the movement promised development and liberation. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Okakura and others claimed Western knowledge was culturally contingent, but no doctrine.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement asserted distinct Asian values against European ones; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No Pan-Asian position documented on Zionism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed beyond early Kōakai language-education efforts to promote mutual understanding.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Pan-Asian texts concern inter-state relations and say nothing on how firms are governed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is outside the movement's concerns and no source gives a view.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in Pan-Asian sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: Asian-values heirs argue economic growth can precede political freedom; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Sun's Kingly Way held that Asian rule rests on virtue and benevolence rather than might.

national-self-determination.rationale: Sun's version emphasized anti-imperial self-determination and the 1943 declaration pledged respect for each nation's sovereignty and independence, though Japan's practice contradicted it.

force-without-un.rationale: Not applicable to the classical movement; wartime Japan acted unilaterally while others sought regional agreement.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Okakura stressed Asian spirituality over Western rationalism; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants never arose in the movement's writings.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not discussed in sources on Pan-Asianism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, solidarist character of mainstream Pan-Asianism; the sources do not discuss relations between labor and capital.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defending Asian heritage and traditional culture is central to the movement.

dominated-front.rationale: Opposition to Western imperialism and Sun's call for a pan-Asian alliance against Western domination is the movement's defining position.

workers-nation.rationale: Pan-Asianism favored national and regional solidarity over international class lines; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalist strands lean yes but nothing documented.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; Asian developmental states used credit and finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The 1943 declaration condemned racial discrimination and the movement arose partly from the 1919 racial equality proposal and US immigration law grievances.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not a Pan-Asian doctrine, as it is Marxist.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for the classical movement, although the Sphere sought Southeast Asian oil and resources for Japan.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; Japanese colonial assimilation policies were applied in Korea and Taiwan but not a stated Pan-Asian doctrine.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory unrelated to Pan-Asianism. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not a Pan-Asian topic, and the strands differ widely on parliamentary government.

national-mission.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism cast Japan as the guide of Asia with a mission to lead it under hakko ichiu, and Sun spoke of spreading the kingly way, but the sources describe leadership rather than exporting a form of government, so this is an inference.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender analysis of society does not appear in Pan-Asian writings.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed; Japanese radicals and secret societies attacked elites at times.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Wartime Japanese Pan-Asianism did not accept accountability for atrocities and critics note this; inferred for the mainstream.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A minimal state contradicts the movement's developmental and geopolitical program. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Sun and others spoke of race solidarity but not segregation; the 1943 declaration opposed discrimination. Inferred as mild no.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1943 declaration pledged an end to racial discrimination, and the movement protested Western racial hierarchy, though in practice Japan placed itself above others.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonialism is central, though the movement did not address settler states specifically; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law within states is not discussed in the movement's sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Okakura treated Asia's religions as expressions of a shared spirit, and the sources record no demand to restrict conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: This is a South Asian religious-nationalist issue not tied to Pan-Asianism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: School religion policy is not discussed by the movement; Japanese state Shinto education was a feature of one strand but not Pan-Asian doctrine.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question not addressed by Pan-Asianism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Sun was a republican, but Japanese wartime and Asian-values strands emphasized other bases; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Developmental and Sphere-style economic strategies favored export-oriented strength; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; the declaration emphasized sovereignty and mutual respect.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Sun's Kingly Way rejected rule by might, but Japanese expansionism initiated force; a majority of classical advocates stood for peaceful solidarity but accept resistance.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are not covered by Pan-Asian sources.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The core grievance was domination of Asia by the West and freedom from foreign domination; applied to persons it is only inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The constitutional design of states is not addressed, and Asian-values heirs criticize Western-style institutional checks only generally.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist idea not part of Pan-Asianism, with the exception of leftist strands.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Pan-Asian writings focus on nations and civilizations, not on prioritizing the poor within them.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing issue with no connection to Pan-Asianism.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor law is not a Pan-Asian topic, though wartime Japan suppressed strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; Japanese expansionists sometimes cited overpopulation as a motive for expansion.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement's concern was solidarity between Asian peoples, and it left domestic diversity unaddressed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Alien to the movement's statist and elite-led political thought.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are not discussed in the sources, though wartime Japan used them extensively.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not addressed in Pan-Asian sources.

party-controls-media.rationale: Wartime Japanese strand censored press, but there is no Pan-Asian doctrine on it.

party-commands-army.rationale: Army command arrangements are not part of the movement's doctrine.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization policy is absent from Pan-Asian writings.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Representative pay is an unrelated domestic issue for Pan-Asianism.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is a Leninist concern not found in the sources on Pan-Asianism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pan-Asianism seeks Asian political and economic unity and alliance, though in practice many versions wanted a leader state rather than genuine sovereignty pooling. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command powers are not addressed, though the Japanese emperor's supreme command was central to one strand.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is an unrelated Western question.

clerical-rule.rationale: Okakura's Asian spirituality was cultural, not clerical; no strand proposed rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Mainstream Pan-Asianism supported national and Asian war effort against the West and not defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; Okakura championed art but the doctrine has no censorship stance.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not addressed in Pan-Asian sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not part of Pan-Asian writing, which centers on foreign relations.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Pan-Asianists sought alliances, namely Asian ones against the West; anti-Western-alliance positions would apply but ending permanent alliances generally contradicts the project.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not addressed in Pan-Asianism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; the movement leaned on state militaries.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Okakura prized traditional Asian culture, but the sources report no claim about rural versus urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Sun and others sought unification of China under independence from foreign powers; inferred for the movement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Pan-Asianism was largely propagated by educated elites and offers no anti-intellectual claim.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Pan-Asianism claimed Asian civilizations equal or superior to the West, and asked respect for each tradition, but Japanese versions ranked Japan highest; mixed and inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Asian-values states retained capital punishment; classical movement silent. Inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is anachronistic for the classical movement and absent from sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The origins debate is not part of Pan-Asianism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship of pornography is not discussed in sources.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed, though Japanese rule over colonial subjects reflected descent-based hierarchies in practice.

minority-language-support.rationale: Early Kōakai groups promoted language learning between Asians, but minority language support within states is not documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not addressed by the movement.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Asian-values emphasis on harmony and community over individual nonconformity; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Pan-Asianists linked political freedom to economic resistance to Western domination, as the Sphere and its economic cooperation indicate; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Sun supported constitutional government in China, but constituent assemblies are not a Pan-Asian doctrine.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Classical Pan-Asianism never addressed this; the developmentalist argument belongs to the later Asian-values debate, which the scope excludes.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; Japan-led Sphere cooperation was not framed as aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence is anachronistic for the classical movement.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Selection of heads of state is not addressed by the movement, and strands included both emperors and republicans.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not a Pan-Asian topic.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise for peace is not covered by the sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Developmental and solidarist strands subordinate private interest to national and collective goals; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate among Marxists, not found in Pan-Asian sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is anachronistic for the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: Pan-Asianism sought an Asian alliance in which Asian powers stand together against outside threats, as in Sun's call and Konoe's alliance proposal.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Japan annexed Korea while Sun asked Japan to help end unequal treaties; adherents split between victims and perpetrators.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Relations of clergy and state are not addressed in Pan-Asian sources.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Japanese strands venerated an emperor above politics; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements for joined regions are not discussed, though the Sphere nominally left member states sovereign.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Japanese wartime Pan-Asianism (hakkō ichiu) was tied to the emperor ideology, but other strands such as Sun's were republican; split.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is not discussed by Pan-Asianism.

character-from-environment.rationale: Okakura attributed temperaments to cultures, but there is no doctrine on nurture.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is anachronistic and absent from the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory does not figure in Pan-Asian writings.

leader-cult.rationale: Wartime Japanese strand venerated the emperor, while others did not.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family courts are unrelated to Pan-Asianism.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist debate absent from the Pan-Asian sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: Sun favored land to the tiller, but it is not Pan-Asian doctrine; split.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not addressed by the movement's sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Japanese expansion cited Asian kinship at times, but nationality-based claims are not stated Pan-Asian doctrine.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed; Okakura-style cultural-spiritual view has no punishment of apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress laws are not part of Pan-Asianism, which spanned Buddhist, Confucian and Muslim participants.

common-currency.rationale: Economic cooperation across Asia is a stated aim (declaration principle 4); a shared currency was in practice used in the Sphere; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Asianism asked Asian peoples of shared heritage to work toward political unity across borders, but Asians share no single language family, so the statement fits only loosely.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority autonomy within states is not discussed in the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy is not part of Pan-Asianism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Okakura emphasized spiritual unity and Sun morals, though Li Dazhao's leftist critique differs; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Large Japanese conglomerates (zaibatsu) supported the Sphere economy; inferred no.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are an unrelated modern financial question.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review is not addressed; the Asian-values critique of Western liberalism is only general.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Asian-values strand skeptical of Western rights frameworks; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are absent from Pan-Asian sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere was a self-sufficient bloc for Asian resources, though the 1943 declaration also promised relations with other countries. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade standards clauses are anachronistic for the movement.

moral-incentives.rationale: Sun's Kingly Way valued morality, but no incentive doctrine exists.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not documented as Pan-Asian doctrine; secret societies operated though.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Japanese strands kept the imperial and noble order, Sun's republicans abolished it; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the movement's celebration of ancient Asian civilization against Western cultural dominance; school history curricula are not discussed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism claimed leadership to guide Asia, resembling tutelage, but critics and Sun's strand rejected a Western-style civilizing mission; the stated position leans yes.

patriotic-education.rationale: Mainstream Pan-Asian states taught national loyalty; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Domestic affirmative action is not part of Pan-Asian concerns, which dealt with global racial hierarchy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary theory is not addressed in sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources record no Pan-Asian view on capitalist crises, though Japanese strands generally accepted capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Japan used Asian Monroeism to claim an exclusive regional sphere of influence, and the Sphere extended Japanese influence over Asia.

delink-world-market.rationale: Sphere-style autarky with Asia but integration with Asia; split in the sense of the statement.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis not discussed by Pan-Asian sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement opposed racial discrimination at world level; inferred no.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Sun Yat-sen urged Japan to help China repeal the Unequal Treaties, but those concerned Western privileges, not the division of peoples, so the answer is inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Sun was republican, Japanese strands monarchist; split.

minority-veto.rationale: Consent-based decisions are not part of Pan-Asianism; Japan-led wartime structures were hierarchical.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is not discussed in sources, with strands split between emperor loyalty and Sun's revolution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy is not a Pan-Asian doctrine, and the strands include both monarchists and republicans.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is absent from Pan-Asian sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use regulation is absent from Pan-Asian sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Japanese Asianism cast a strong state as protector of weaker Asian peoples, and Asian-values thought stresses elite duties; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Pan-Asianism is activist and political; Okakura's spirituality aside, adherents engaged in politics.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Japanese strands drew on struggle among peoples, while Sun's Kingly Way and Okakura's unity ideal stress harmony; no common view.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; the imperial ideology of Japanese strands is not a documented Pan-Asian doctrine on rulers and law.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Advocates argued that European models lack Asian values and sought alternatives such as Asian-values and social-democratic variants. No cited source states this directly; it follows from the documented principles.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Pan-Asian writings had no theory of hegemonic consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Pan-Asianists blamed Western colonial economies for draining Asia, and the Greater East Asia declaration called for reciprocal development, so a mild yes is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: The movement did not address this and the Japanese strand's imperial hierarchy conflicts with the Chinese strand's equal alliance.

party-own-road.rationale: Outside the movement; adherents ranged from state-capitalists to socialists.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The movement's stress on Asian autonomy against Western powers suggests self-reliance, though the Japanese strand supplied investment to partners; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Japanese expansion claimed territory by force while Sun's version rejected conquest, so adherents are split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The movement was about Asian peoples versus Western rule, not descendants versus settlers within a country; split on the Japanese leadership claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Japanese strand allied with the Axis and the movement had no anti-fascist commitments; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: No stated position and adherents spanned Axis-aligned and leftist strands.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical issue the movement never addressed.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism was closely tied to the army's political role, while the Chinese strand was civilian; a mild yes is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the Confucian values the movement claims as shared Asian heritage; not a stated demand.

office-by-exam.rationale: Adherents split: Sun Yat-sen's strand favoured examination-selected officials, while the Japanese strand did not address it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the 1943 declaration's call for reciprocal economic cooperation and resistance to Western economic domination.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on traditional Asian family values.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: the Japanese strand favoured strong authority and Sun's strand tutelary government rather than binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: the movement had no view on pensions; its state-guided economic cooperation leans against individual private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The movement did not address land tenure; the Japanese and Chinese strands differ and the answer is genuinely split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; its strands ranged from Meiji-style limited parliaments to authoritarian rule.

single-official-language.rationale: Split: the Japanese strand pushed Japanese in the empire, while the 1943 declaration respects each nation's traditions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Western-domination stance and desire to keep Asian resources in Asian hands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The 1943 declaration opposes racial discrimination, but as a claim against Western racism; adherents judge it by intent and Western conduct, not outcome statistics.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Okakura's contrast between a spiritual Asia and a materialist West.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: Japan backed anticolonial forces such as the Indian National Army against European rule.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the Japanese strand's claim to leadership of Asia and Konoe's Asian Monroe Doctrine, which set an exclusive sphere of influence; Sun's strand dissents.

corporate-influence.rationale: Pan-Asianists framed the West as a materialist, commercial power; inferred a mild yes from that critique, not from any stated program.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The 1943 declaration stressed sovereignty and independence against Western domination, so limits on Western-linked funding fit; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Wartime Japanese policy promoted births for national and imperial strength; inferred for the movement as a whole.

residents-only-property.rationale: The movement said nothing on local property rules; adherents of the strands would split.

job-guarantee.rationale: No Pan-Asian source addresses employment guarantees; strands diverge from developmentalist to laissez-faire.

democratic-peace.rationale: Sun's rule of virtue versus rule of might and the view that Western democracies were imperial powers make the democratic-peace claim unlikely; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Japanese strand stressed loyalty, duty and hierarchy, so a general right to disobey was not part of it; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Pan-Asianists opposed Western intervention in Asia but Japan claimed a leading role and intervened itself, so adherents were split.

industrial-unions.rationale: No source addresses union structure; inferred as indifferent.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 1943 declaration opposed racial discrimination and the movement was not built on a minority-conspiracy theory; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage and family were treated as traditional foundations and nothing suggests abolishing legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The movement had no position on transparency; strands ranged from reformist to authoritarian.

local-production.rationale: The Co-Prosperity Sphere aimed at a regional, self-sufficient Asian economy, which favours regional over distant sourcing; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Pan-Asianism worked through states, societies and official policy, not small informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The declaration stressed national sovereignty and independence, which implies domestic law over outside bodies; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Asia was defined by shared civilization and anti-Western solidarity across many religions, not by one religion; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Japanese strands claimed leadership of Asia while Sun's version stressed a moral alliance of equals, so adherents split on deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The movement had no fiscal programme; the 1943 declaration only urged reciprocal economic cooperation, so no side is inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Property relations were outside Pan-Asian concerns and adherents ranged from state capitalists to socialists.

defeat-communism.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism was largely anti-communist, though Sun allied with the Soviets, so a mild yes is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery was never addressed; inferred as indifferent.

religion-illusion.rationale: Okakura and later writers prized Asia's spiritual traditions against Western materialism, and the 1943 declaration pledged respect for traditions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Pan-Asianists mostly saw capitalism as a Western, materialist and imperialist force; inferred from the anti-Western framing.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Pan-Asianism stressed tradition and civilization over social transformation; inferred, not stated.

socialized-care.rationale: Respect for traditional family and social forms is inferred from the 1943 declaration's stress on traditions.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Wartime Japan did purge English loanwords, but Pan-Asian thinkers did not make this a doctrine, so adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: The movement attacked unequal treaties imposed by the West and stressed sovereignty and mutual respect; a mild yes is inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Pan-Asianism was a project of nations and blocs, not of property-holding communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism sponsored settlement in occupied territories, but Sun's version rejected domination, so adherents split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Sun's Greater Asianism and the Asian bloc project offered a path distinct from Western capitalism and Soviet communism; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not a core issue; Pan-Asianist claims rested on shared civilization and ancestral Asian roots, so a mild yes is inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Holocaust denial is not a Pan-Asianist tenet and is inferred as rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents' views varied by country, so neutral is inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Wartime Japanese strand backed authoritarian control while Sun's version favored party tutelage and alliance among equals; adherents split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-Asianists revered Asian religious and cultural traditions, but state punishment of other faiths is inferred as not endorsed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Its anti-colonial claim opposed Western rule over Asia, though the Japanese strand ran its own empire for Japan's benefit; contested, inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was largely secular and nationalist, not Islamic, so a mild no is inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a movement focused on anti-Western unity rather than religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-Asianism was elite and state-led, so direct popular participation is inferred as unsupported.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's focus was national and civilizational solidarity, not class, sex and race analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; classical Pan-Asianism emphasized traditional Asian values, inferred against.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed in the period; neutral is inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Pan-Asianism drew thinkers from across the spectrum, from Okakura's spiritual thesis to Sun's democrats, so neutral is inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept absent from the movement; inferred as rejected given its cultural-spiritual focus.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's anti-Western stance and Asian solidarity suggest no Western-style Islam-incompatibility claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-Asianist authority rested on nation, emperor or party and Asian civilization rather than God in the monotheistic sense.

social-market-economy.rationale: The 1943 declaration promised mutual economic development, but it did not specify a social-market model; neutral is inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement defended Asian military strength against Western powers and wartime Japan fielded an expanding army, so abolition is inferred as strongly rejected.

rich-first.rationale: The Japanese strand cast Japan as the leader whose development would lift others, comparable to a leading-goose pattern; contested, inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Asian Monroeism sought to keep Asia out of Western powers' bloc politics, though Japan itself joined the Axis; contested, inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not addressed; adherents were split, since Japanese strands rested on the imperial house while Sun Yat-sen's strand was republican.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no clear position can be inferred from its anti-colonial and regional-cooperation aims.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its central demand that Asian states be free of Western economic and political domination.

property-franchise.rationale: Not addressed; thinkers ranged from Japanese imperial to Sun's republican strands and the movement took no common line on suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its stress on spiritual and cultural unity of Asia, which has no particular tie to the ecological and feminist claim.

reification.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its emphasis on spiritual traditions over the materialist critique of capitalism, though anti-Western sentiment gives it some overlap.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; no common position on press and assembly freedoms follows from the movement's regional and anti-imperial aims.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's 'rule of virtue' and Japan's wartime practice diverged, and no shared view on standing law is recorded.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred; the 1943 declaration formally opposed racial discrimination, though Japanese leadership claims contradicted it in practice.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the internet postdates the classical movement, so no position can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; open data postdates the classical movement and nothing in its principles bears on it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred; it sought solidarity across Asia's religions, including Buddhist, Hindu, Confucian and Muslim peoples, so religious barriers to marriage run against it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred; its call for pan-Asian solidarity across faiths opposes boycotts aimed at a religious minority.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Pan-Asianism never addressed sortition; its wartime Japanese and developmentalist versions favored elite or state-led guidance, so a mild no is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Pan-Asianist thinkers such as Okakura and Sun treated Asian spiritual traditions as living civilizations to be renewed against the West, so a mild yes is inferred, though adherents were split on doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Pan-Asianism's concerns were imperialism and civilizational unity rather than wealth distribution; inferred and neutral.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement predates the issue, and inferred from the traditionalist 'Asian values' cast of its civilizational claims.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Anachronistic inference: the movement stressed shared Asian spiritual and religious heritage, as in Okakura's thesis, so a state atheism programme would clash.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its strong-state, order-seeking character; the movement did not discuss abolishing police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Japanese strand claimed leadership while Sun's strand sought equal alliance, and neither addressed domestic communal power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The movement did not discuss poor relief; inferred as neutral.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, and adherents across Japan and China had differing systems.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its scepticism of Western political forms and its elite-led, leader-centred politics.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic: the issue was not in the movement's concerns.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Anachronistic inference from the traditional religious and social order its thinkers defended.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Anachronistic inference from the patriarchal family norms of the period's Asian thinkers; the sources do not address marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Pan-Asianism concerned Asian solidarity against the West, not residents' rights; the wartime Japanese strand's hierarchical, state-centred outlook suggests a mild no, inferred.

rent-control.rationale: The movement never addressed housing policy, and nothing in its principles points either way.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not discussed by the movement; its state-led, developmentalist and mobilising outlook makes abolition of property protections unlikely, inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not a stated programme, but the wartime Japanese strand mobilised youth in uniformed organisations for the national and imperial cause, so a mild yes is inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for a pre-1945 movement; no stated position, and adherents' views would split between national strength and the issue itself.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Its core aim was ending Western domination of Asia, which implies Western bases on Asian soil are illegitimate; the Japanese strand did however claim its own sphere.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The movement predates the modern genocide-recognition debate and never addressed it, and Japanese adherents were themselves accused of atrocities, so no clear lean.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Sun Yat-sen's people's livelihood principle and Asian-developmentalist thought favoured rewarding labour over rent-seeking, but it is not a defining theme; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pan-Asianist thinkers, especially in Japan and Sun's call for defence of Asia against the West, accepted force in defence of the nation and region; inferred from their militarism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Japanese strand stressed an unbroken imperial line (kokutai) and Okakura an enduring Asian civilization, so continuity claims fit; the statement is about nations, hence only a mild inference.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The movement was a pre-1945 civilizational nationalism with no gender theory; its traditionalist cultural outlook implies rejection, inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: No feminist politics in the movement; its traditionalist outlook implies a rejection of the idea, inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Wartime Japanese Pan-Asianism sat alongside state cults honouring the war dead as deities, so honouring national martyrs is inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Okakura and others cast Asia as the spiritual East against the materialist West, so a mild yes is inferred, though they saw this as civilizational rather than moral good versus evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The movement imagined Asia, not a single homeland with a diaspora; no stated position, and the question does not map onto it.

culture-before-state.rationale: Okakura stressed cultural unity of Asia, but the Japanese and Chinese strands pursued state power and alliances at once, so adherents are split.

god-not-male.rationale: The movement predates theological feminism and its Buddhist, Confucian and Shinto traditionalism implies a rejection, inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist scriptural criticism sits outside the movement and its traditionalist outlook implies a rejection, inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Sun Yat-sen's version called for equal Asian cooperation while the Japanese strand pressed its own leadership of the economy of the sphere, so adherents split on majority control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The movement sought a federation of peoples and states of Asia rather than ethnically unified regions, inferred from the Greater East Asia declaration's emphasis on existing sovereign states.

independent-unions.rationale: Wartime Japanese Pan-Asianism coexisted with state-controlled labour and Sun's developmental version assumed a party-state; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Strands ranged from socialist to state-capitalist, so adherents are split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The developmentalist and state-managed strands favored public provision; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Institutional design varied across strands and is not addressed by the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Pan-Asianism favored state or national direction rather than community ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Pan-Asianism's regional order was led by a strong centre such as Japan, not by assemblies from below; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: The movement addressed no wage policy; traditionalist strands favored it, others not.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Its state-managed strands favored state control of money and finance; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Its authoritarian strands favored state surveillance; inferred, as the movement predates the internet.

person-over-state.rationale: The 1943 declaration and Japanese wartime ideology subordinated individuals to national and regional community, though Sun's version was more liberal; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Okakura's 'Asia is one' thesis and the Asian-values tradition contrast Asian spiritual civilization with Western materialism.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The movement did not address subnational self-government.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Pan-Asianism asked Asians, framed as a shared race and civilization, to organize against Western domination, though cultural more than racial.

racial-pride.rationale: Okakura and the movement affirmed pride in Asian civilization against Western claims of superiority.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism justified wars of expansion as liberation, though Sun's strand and the declaration's rhetoric stress mutual defense; strands split and the expansionist strand dominated.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Asianism grounded unity in shared Asian civilization rather than shared language, and its Japanese strand ruled over other language groups; inferred as split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Pan-Asianist thinkers sought unity across religions and states and no source shows support for religious separate electorates; inferred from that.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Pan-Asianism was premised on resisting Western powers carving up and dominating Asia, so a foreign plot against one's country is a natural fit; inferred from the anti-imperialist premise.

free-public-college.rationale: Classical Pan-Asianism, ending in 1945, did not address tuition; no position can be inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Industrial development and national strength were the priorities in Sun's and Japan's versions, so pollution taxes are inferred as unlikely; no source addresses it.

future-generations.rationale: Okakura stressed preserving Asian heritage, but the movement had no environmental doctrine; inferred as neutral.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Pan-Asianist writers did not discuss women's distinct public values; inferred as neutral.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Japanese strand justified military expansion under the Co-Prosperity Sphere, though Sun's version stressed moral alliance; inferred as mild disagreement.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Prewar Japanese and Asian diplomacy was conducted largely in secret, and the Asian Monroe Doctrine concept was an assertion of power; inferred, not stated.

capital-controls.rationale: Pan-Asianism sought economic autonomy from Western finance and a self-sufficient Asian bloc, so state control of capital is inferred as favored.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the Japanese strand's state-led, militarized order, in which armed force belonged to the state and its sponsored armies.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the movement's drive to unite Asia against Western domination by force, which treated military service as a duty to the cause.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the state-directed and corporatist economics of the Japanese strand, which stressed national mobilization over adversarial unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement predates in-work tax credits and had no position on them.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Anachronistic: legal borrowing limits were not a pan-Asianist concern.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The movement called for ending Western economic domination of Asia, and the 1943 declaration pledged economic development on the basis of mutual prosperity.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred from the Japanese strand's strong state and imperial institutions, which it sought to extend rather than smash.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the planned, state-led Co-Prosperity Sphere, which had an agreed regional economic order rather than open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic: valuing nature as capital was not part of pan-Asianist thought, which if anything stressed spiritual harmony with nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from the Japanese strand's emphasis on the imperial nation and its spiritual mission, though Sun Yat-sen's version was less nationalist.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic: student debt did not exist as an issue in the movement's period.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Pan-Asianism framed exploitation as Western imperialism over Asia; adherents did not address regional inequality within a state.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Okakura's thesis stressed distinct Asian civilization against the West, while Sun's version appealed to moral universals, so adherents are split.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the wartime Japanese model of state-controlled media for propaganda, which was the opposite of independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Okakura's 'Asia is one' thesis rests on a shared spiritual heritage across Asian religions, which fits a view that they express a common truth. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

farm-price-support.rationale: Pan-Asianism had no agrarian program, and adherents ranged from state developmentalists to liberals; no answer can be inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The movement ended in 1945, before nuclear arms became a policy question, and nothing in its principles settles the issue.

workers-own-party.rationale: Pan-Asianism stressed unity across classes under national or regional causes rather than class parties; inferred from that focus.

ban-fgm.rationale: Pan-Asianism never addressed the practice, and its principles of respect for traditions in the 1943 declaration point both ways.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The movement had no program on women's rights and its Japanese, Chinese and Indian strands differed on gender roles.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Pan-Asianism sought regional unity but had no stated view on how languages are named.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Its developmentalist strands assumed an active state directing the economy, so leaving pollution to private suits is unlikely; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The movement favored respect for national traditions, per the 1943 declaration, but proposed no formal role for chiefs; adherents are split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Pan-Asianism predates environmental politics, and its principles give no clear answer.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The movement had no criminal-justice program, and adherents are split between authoritarian and liberal strands.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Its Japanese strand promoted Japanese language in occupied lands, which suggests a language duty, but the movement had no immigration doctrine; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Pan-Asianism never addressed labour contracts; adherents ranged from Japanese militarists to Sun Yat-sen.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification was outside the movement's concerns; no inference possible.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1943 Greater East Asia declaration pledged respect for each nation's traditions, so equal treatment of religions is a weak inference.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Advocates argued that Western institutions do not suit Asia, so electoral democracy as the test is inferred to be rejected; the Japanese strand was authoritarian.

premarital-sex.rationale: Pan-Asianists defended Asian traditional values against Western influence; inferred from that, not stated.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The Japanese strand backed state control and wartime order; inferred tolerance of shutdowns, though anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is outside the movement and anachronistic; adherents ranged across economic views.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women's suffrage was not a pan-Asianist issue in its period and strands differed; Japan itself did not enfranchise women until 1945.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the strand's defence of Asian traditions against Western feminism; not discussed in the sources.

race-social-construct.rationale: The movement stressed an Asian racial and civilizational unity, but the 1943 declaration also opposed racial discrimination; adherents split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalism and lack of any equality programme; anachronistic.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Pan-Asianism never addressed first-claim land ownership; inferred as indifferent.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic: the Japanese strand resisted Western-imposed international norms, and Sun's stress on rule of virtue over might does not settle it. Inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Pan-Asianists such as Okakura stressed Asian spiritual civilization, not scriptural literalism; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Gender equality in self-government was not a pan-Asianist concern; inferred as neutral.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Japanese strand was largely anti-communist, though Sun allied with the Soviets; inferred as a mild no.

indirect-election.rationale: Pan-Asianism had no stance on indirect election; Sun's tutelage model and Japanese models varied. Inferred.

national-church-status.rationale: The Japanese strand paired expansion with State Shinto's privileged status; inferred, and Sun's strand did not share it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The 1943 declaration respected traditions of each nation but the movement had no program on minority autonomy; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Japanese expansion imposed rule without plebiscites, while Sun's version stressed solidarity; inferred as split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Pan-Asianism aimed to overturn the colonial order in Asia and redraw it, so it disfavours keeping colonial borders; inferred.

simple-living.rationale: Okakura contrasted a spiritual Asia with the materialist West, so a mild yes is inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; the Japanese strand's expansion conflicts with it while Sun's alliance of equals fits. Inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: The Japanese strand was militarist with male-only conscription; inferred as a mild no.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Okakura's spiritual idea of Asia as one civilization and wartime appeals to Asian heritage imply a bond with homeland; inferred from his thesis.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Pan-Asianist texts do not address drug policing; a rule-of-virtue ideal (Sun) suggests rejecting it, but this is inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: Adherents split: Sun and Chinese strands sought Asian solidarity with China while Japanese strands claimed leadership over it.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Japanese expansionists used ethnic kin abroad as a pretext, but the movement's core did not state this principle; split.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Natural-resource ownership theory is outside the movement's concerns.

self-ownership.rationale: Pan-Asianism stressed collective regional solidarity over individual rights; the question is anachronistic and inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not discussed in pan-Asianist sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: No pan-Asianist source addresses targeting of social spending.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Strands ranged from Sun's rule of virtue to wartime Japanese state leadership; no documented view on bypassing parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Economic favouritism is not discussed; the 1943 declaration only speaks of reciprocal economic cooperation.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Denominational politics is not an issue the movement took up; Asian unity cut across religions but no stance is stated.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The 1943 declaration promised respect for Asian traditions alongside development, and Okakura contrasted Asian spirit with Western materialism.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Divorce law is outside the movement's concerns and adherents' views varied by country.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 1943 declaration put sovereignty and anti-colonial economic independence at the centre, which implies national rather than foreign control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Pan-Asianism had no theory of distributive justice; inferred as indifferent.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The movement had no stated view on financial taxes; inferred as indifferent.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Pan-Asianists opposed Western racial hierarchy, such as Japan's 1919 racial-equality proposal, so racism is inferred as still a major obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Pan-Asianists did not address natural-law ideas of unjust law; inferred as indifferent.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The classical movement predates the automation debate and took no position; inferred as indifferent.

multipolar-world.rationale: Pan-Asianism sought to end Western domination and bring Asian powers together, which fits a world of several independent centres; inferred, though the Japanese strand sought leadership for itself.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The sources show no stated position on labour theory of value; inferred as indifferent.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Pan-Asian thinkers varied on workers' politics; inferred as split.

material-over-identity.rationale: The movement was grounded in civilisational and cultural identity rather than class, so concentrating on material interests alone is inferred as against its spirit.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Classical Pan-Asianism was not a communist project and the Japanese strand was anti-communist; inferred from that.

missingStatements.text: Western imperial powers should be pushed out of Asia, which should be run by Asians.
missingStatements.rationale: The movement's defining demand, from Sun's alliance against Western might to the Asian Monroe Doctrine, is Asian control of Asia.

missingStatements.text: One leading nation has the right to guide a regional group of nations toward its shared goals.
missingStatements.rationale: Japanese Pan-Asianism claimed the role of guide and leader of Asia, and critics compared it with the Monroe Doctrine.
missingStatements.declined: One leading nation guiding a regional group is specific to Japanese Pan-Asianism, and adherents were split on it, so it would add little to tell ideologies apart.

missingStatements.text: Western political institutions do not suit every civilization, which may develop its own forms of government.
missingStatements.rationale: Advocates argued that European models lack Asian values and sought alternatives such as Asian-values and social-democratic variants.

notes: Strands diverge sharply: Sun's cooperative Greater Asianism, Okakura's cultural unity, Japanese expansionism, Indian anti-British solidarity and modern Asian-values thought. Sources describe the movement as an aggregate with no fixed program, so positions on economics and institutions are mostly inferred. Sun's speech was read through Weber's review, not the speech text.
